findings.cross_file_justification: The diff's _measured() predicate is what lets the suite accept the new claude-opus-5-5 catalog entry (effective_input_ceiling 936000, ceiling_calibration.transport: claude-headless, cli_model: global.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5). That field on an auth_type: http_api entry is consumed by cheval._lookup_max_input_tokens / loa_cheval.routing.ceiling.input_bound to gate direct Anthropic HTTP dispatch, and the diff's test_legacy_wall_applies_only_to_anthropic_under_the_kill_switch now asserts the HTTP gate equals that CLI-measured value.
findings.description: _measured() honors any operator_set/empirical_probe calibration with calibrated_at, with no check that ceiling_calibration.transport matches the entry's dispatch path. The only measured entry it admits was probed through `claude -p` over Bedrock (transport claude-headless), yet it is the http_api entry whose ceiling moved from 180K (which the same test's docstring says was 'probed under streaming' on the HTTP route) to 936K. The HTTP route's account_limits remain tier: unverified, itpm: null, so nothing on the HTTP transport has demonstrated acceptance of a 936K-token request.
findings.failure_mode: cheval's walk gate now admits HTTP requests to claude-opus-5-5 between 180K and 936K input tokens. If the direct API account rejects them (400 prompt-too-long, 429 ITPM, or a tier gate on the 1M window), the call fails after the payload is built and falls back to anthropic:claude-opus-5 whose ceiling is still 180K, so the fallback cannot carry the same request either. The suite stays green because the test follows the catalog value rather than a transport-matched measurement.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the calibration transport-aware: in _measured (and ideally in input_bound) only treat a calibration as governing an http_api entry when cal.get('transport') is absent or 'api'; add an assertion in test_every_http_entry_has_ceiling_with_provenance that a calibrated http_api entry's transport is compatible with auth_type. Alternatively run the probe's --transport api path once for claude-opus-5-5 on the HTTP route before raising the HTTP ceiling, and record the headless measurement under the entry that actually dispatches through the CLI.

findings.description: For measured entries `cap = entry['effective_input_ceiling']`, so `expected = min(effective, cw - dmt)` and the assertion `effective == expected` reduces to the I1 check on the next line: the test is tautological for exactly the entries the cycle introduced, and the recorded measurement (ceiling_calibration.measured_input_tokens 972887) is never compared to the written 936000. test_legacy_wall_applies_only_to_anthropic_under_the_kill_switch likewise derives `want` from _measured(), a test-local reimplementation of the runtime's calibrated predicate that already diverges from input_bound in two ways: it filters on source (kf_derived + calibrated_at is 'calibrated' to the runtime per test_i1_and_i2_per_entry_from_the_fields but not to _measured), and it ignores stale_after_days. The module already has the right pattern in test_walk_gate_threshold_is_the_policy_bound_not_the_literal, which asks input_bound for the expected value.
findings.failure_mode: The I2 clamp the report says the lead applied by hand (and which the tool's clean path previously omitted) is unchecked against the measurement: a future write of probed_ceiling/effective_input_ceiling = measured_input_tokens that happens to satisfy I1 (e.g. a smaller max_tokens default) would pass. Any future divergence between _measured() and input_bound (a kf_derived calibration with a non-180K value, or staleness handling in the runtime after 2027-01-05 for the current entry) flips test_legacy_wall_applies_only_to_anthropic_under_the_kill_switch red or, worse, keeps it green while the gate serves a different number than the test believes.
findings.suggested_fix: For measured entries assert `effective_input_ceiling == min(cal['measured_input_tokens'], context_window - _default_max_tokens(entry))` and `probed_ceiling == effective_input_ceiling`; compute `want` in the legacy-wall test via `input_bound(entry, max_tokens=_default_max_tokens(entry)).value` instead of _measured(), and keep _measured() only for the shape checks in test_opus_5_5_has_the_1m_window_at_standard_pricing.

findings.description: The module-scoped guard asserts that .run/model-invoke.jsonl (cheval's MODELINV ledger) is byte-identical before and after the module, and the docstring presents this as proof that 'no live call escaped the fake'. On the claude-headless transport the probe spawns ${CLAUDE_HEADLESS_BIN:-claude} directly via subprocess (record['argv'] == [bin, *PINNED]); a real `claude -p` never writes cheval's ledger, so the guard cannot observe the one spend path this module exercises. test_runs_from_another_cwd_under_python_isolated_mode builds its own environment rather than using the `fake` fixture, so a future edit that drops the CLAUDE_HEADLESS_BIN assignment there would run the real CLI with --budget-usd 20 and still satisfy the guard.
findings.failure_mode: A test that reaches the real CLI bisects a 400K-token Opus 5.5 prompt for up to the $20 budget per test, on the operator's Bedrock/API account, and the module reports zero live spend.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the guard fail-closed for this transport: at module setup set CLAUDE_HEADLESS_BIN to a non-existent path (and PATH to an empty dir for the PATH test) so any test that forgets the fake fails on spawn; and/or have each test assert that fake['calls']() is non-empty and that record['cli_bin'] equals the fake path. Keep the ledger check only where the API transport is exercised.

findings.description: The test pins the budget pre-flight at 'worst-case step ≈ $1.60' for a 400K-token step and '12 such steps fit in $20', i.e. input_per_mtok ($4/MTok) only. The fake, like the real CLI, reports the prompt under usage.cache_creation_input_tokens, which the Anthropic API bills at 1.25× input, so the worst-case step is ≈$2.00 and only 10 such steps fit in $20. The record labels this pricing_basis: catalog_estimate.
findings.failure_mode: If the budget gate stops on the catalog estimate rather than the CLI's total_cost_usd, a run of all-accepted steps can spend ≈$25 against a $20 --budget-usd before the tool declares the budget exhausted; the live run happened to under-spend only because CLI-preflight rejections cost nothing while being estimated at full price.
findings.suggested_fix: Price cache_creation_input_tokens at 1.25× input in the estimate (or add cache_write_per_mtok to the catalog and read it), prefer the CLI's total_cost_usd for the running total when present, and update the pinned strings to the corrected figures.
